Armed Conflict & Security
• An Oregon primary school attack ended when a teacher tackled the 16-year-old suspect targeting a special-needs classroom, and an armed parent shot the assailant, police said.
• Three men were sentenced to 158 years each for murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and American surfer Carter Rhoad in a botched robbery in Mexico.
• Sudan’s army and the RSF traded claims after clashes in Nyala; the army said dozens of RSF fighters were killed, while the RSF accused the army of killing 30 civilians at a livestock market.
• Yemen’s Houthi forces struck Aden’s presidential palace and airport and have encircled Taiz, escalating their conflict with Saudi-backed forces.
• Masked Israeli settlers assaulted Palestinians and a U.S. photojournalist during an olive harvest in the occupied West Bank, injuring several people.
Why it matters: Intensifying regional conflicts and flashpoints—from Yemen and Sudan to the West Bank—underscore rising instability, while domestic security incidents highlight persistent vulnerabilities and community responses.

• Senator Rubio’s Uzbekistan visit highlights Central Asia’s search for diverse partners, while Japan’s PM Takaichi plans to attend APEC in China if parliament permits.

• Croatian authorities made arrests over pro-Nazi chants at a Hajduk Split–Ajax match.

Climate & Environment
• Brazil’s Amazon deforestation fell to a record low ahead of a pivotal election, a reversal from prior years of accelerated loss.
• Scientists warn the Thwaites “Doomsday” glacier may be melting faster than thought, risking accelerated sea-level rise.
• Santa Ana winds fueled a fast-moving Orange County wildfire, prompting thousands of evacuation orders.
• Honeybees, boosted by beekeeping, are displacing wild pollinators at flowers, threatening biodiversity.
• The UN loss and damage fund is set to allocate $20m to Nepal for flood recovery.
Why it matters: From rainforest policy to polar ice and wildfire response, decisions now will shape biodiversity, climate resilience, and vulnerable communities’ recovery for years.

Geopolitics & Diplomacy.text:
For more than three decades, Michael Gove has been a leading figure in British Conservatism. As a journalist, government minister and now editor of the Tory bible, the Spectator, he has helped shape the right even as it has moved further rightwards. In the latest episode of Radical Thinking, Gove joins Aditya Chakrabortty to discuss the future of the right, his record on Brexit and austerity, and the Spectator’s position on IslamWatch the full episode with Michael Gove here.
 
 
 Aditya’s suggested reading:To read the fruits of Michael Gove’s dalliance with the Marxism Today gang, look up his essay in a 1998 collection called The Moderniser’s Dilemma: Radical Politics in the Age of BlairFor slalom ride through Michael Gove’s years in power, read The Demented Dalek by the historian Richard J Evans in the London Review of BooksTo learn more on what’s become of the British right, there’s a column by me for the GuardianJust why the most successful political party is now failing is analysed in-depth by Phil Burton-Cartledge in his book The Party’s Over: The Rise and Fall of the Conservatives from Thatcher to SunakPhil also writes a very good blog on British politics, which keeps a close eye on how each party is trying to marshall a coalition of voters. Here he is on Kemi BadenochGeoffrey Wheatcroft does an entertaining short narrative in Bloody Panico!:or, Whatever Happened to The Tory PartyFor more on the economics of the Cameron years, this paper is acute on how the Tories failed to move the UK away from being a country of renters towards a country of makers. Science & Technology.title: IEEE Offers More Services to Cities That Want to Be Smarter
Science & Technology.text: More and more city governments are using advanced technologies to improve livability for their residents. Municipalities use data from smartphones and sensors for traffic enforcement, traffic control, and waste management. They also have implemented artificial intelligence and deep learning programs.Dubai, Paris, and Coral Gables, Fla., are among the cities that have invested heavily in programs to become smarter.But along with the conveniences that come with a smart city transition, there have been challenges including safety and privacy issues and eroding relationships between residents and city officials.Although many initiatives have delivered real innovations, not all have been successful. Inefficient global coordination has hindered projects with unclear standards, socioeconomic differences, and a lack of worldwide governance, leading to a disconnect between the technologies and the ability to adapt to them.Citizens’ trust in the technologies suffers because of privacy breaches, personal data leaks, and other issues.Finding solutionsSmart city projects are complex and expensive endeavors that involve politicians, citizens, technocrats, and engineers. Successful projects require citizens to be fully engaged and to have strong collaborations with the participants, especially engineers, as engineering is the cornerstone.Collaboration with universities, research institutions, and technology experts can bridge knowledge gaps on the behavior of complex socio-technical systems. What’s missing, though, is a global platform where those involved can discuss their experiences.To help solve those and other challenges, the IEEE Smart Cities Technical Community (formerly the IEEE Smart Cities Initiative) was launched in 2013 by IEEE Future Directions, which incubates emerging technologies and new applications of current ones. The technical community provides city leaders and others with credible, unbiased information and educational content developed by IEEE experts.Since then, IEEE Smart Cities has launched services including its flagship International Smart Cities Conference, a media center with educational and technical resources, and a contest to recognize the best smart project completed by city officials. The platforms bring together practicing engineers, academic researchers, policymakers, and city leaders to collaborate and exchange ideas and experiences about moving toward a smart-city model.Better serving humanityIn 2021 the IEEE Power & Energy Society began managing the Smart Cities program, which is supported by the IEEE Communications, Industry Applications, and Intelligent Transportation Systems societies and other IEEE entities.Thanks to volunteers’ dedication and determination, IEEE Smart Cities launched several services. But the initiative’s structure limited the development of long-term projects and the creation of new activities.To address the situation, the IEEE Technical Activities Board (TAB) created the second-generation technical community ad hoc committee, also in 2021. It was a pilot program whereby IEEE Smart Cities formed a board of governors to oversee the community’s operations and leadership, and created a policies and procedures manual.In November 2025 IEEE Smart Cities became a TAB technical community.IEEE Smart Cities nowToday more than 7,000 volunteers collaborate on various aspects of the community within at least one of the following technical tracks:Smart grid.Smart water management.Green electronics for smart cities.Smart governance and planning.Hydrogen for smart cities.Smart and sustainable campus.Security for smart cities.Smart lighting for cities.Smart mobility for cities.Artificial intelligence for cities.New webinar series, workshops, conferences, educational resources, and other offerings are being created.Two events were launched recently: the IEEE European Technology and Engineering Management Summit, held in May 2025 in Belgium, with the next one planned for 2027; and the IEEE Sustainable Smart Lighting World Conference, scheduled for 2 to 6 December in Athens.The Smart Cities Ambassadors program aims to raise the technical community’s visibility outside IEEE by holding roundtables and other events at non-IEEE functions.IEEE Smart Cities volunteers are working on launching journals. In addition, standards are being developed in collaboration with the IEEE Standards Association, societies, and councils.The program is collaborating with the Open and Agile Smart Cities and Communities network, the Instituto de Competitividad e Innovación para el Desarrollo y Transferencia de Tecnología, and the International Project Management Association. All of those actions have the ultimate objective of boosting IEEE Smart Cities’ growth and sustainability, as well as strengthening the leadership and educational offerings to technical community volunteers.If you would like to volunteer, visit the Smart Cities website.

Science & Technology.title: Simulation App Speeds Up Electric Truck Battery Design
Science & Technology.text: This article is brought to you by COMSOL.These days, no one blinks an eye at two-day, one-day, and even same-day package deliveries. Despite the plethora of localized fulfillment and distribution centers that have cropped up to meet the demand, delivery trucks still need to make considerably long drives, often over highways. To reduce fuel and maintenance costs as well as carbon emissions, companies are investing in electric trucks for their delivery fleets. While turning to electric trucks is a promising solution, the battery packs incorporated into these automotive designs often fall short in the lifetime needed to make long-distance highway travel feasible.To help overcome the issue of battery lifetime, a consortium of universities and industry partners incorporated multiscale simulation and a custom simulation app into the battery manufacturing process. The organizations involved in this project were Aurobay, Resolvent, the European Commission, the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Vinnova (the Swedish Agency for Innovation Systems), Innovation Fund Denmark, and Volvo Group Trucks Operations.The simulation app, built by Resolvent, a Denmark-based engineering consultancy that specializes in green energy, enables the R&D department at Volvo to easily test battery lifetime performance.LaserWho?The Multiscale Simulation of Laser Welding for Optimal Battery Pack Manufacturing project — referred to as “LaserBATMAN” — was initiated in May 2022 and wrapped up in May 2025 (Ref. 1). Although BATMAN here refers to battery manufacturing and not the famous masked superhero, the goals for the project also strove for greatness.The LaserBATMAN project aimed to optimize two key performance metrics for battery packs: robustness and lifetime (Ref. 1). One element of the battery manufacturing process that affects both of these metrics is the laser welding used in component joining processes (for example, to connect battery cells in a pack via a busbar). If done correctly, laser welding can positively impact battery life, but if done incorrectly, laser welding can increase the risk of battery degradation. Computational modeling can be used to analyze and predict the effects of welding and joining processes at different stages of the manufacturing process.Martin Refslund Nielsen, former chief commercial officer and partner at Resolvent, explained that for this type of multiphysics and multiscale problem, “COMSOL Multiphysics is just the right tool.”R&D Workflow for Multiscale Model and AppThe Resolvent team used the COMSOL Multiphysics software to study how laser welding affects the electrochemistry and degradation of battery cells. At least, that’s how the project started.“Ambitions grew,” Nielsen said, explaining that the team ended up modeling the performance of the entire battery, from cell to pack level, and even “turned [the model] into a design tool in the end”, in reference to the app.After training the deep neural network of the battery model, the team built a custom simulation app to efficiently optimize busbar tabs in the configuration of a battery pack.First, the team built an electrochemical model of a battery cell by inputting the formulas for the relevant chemical reaction kinetics (Figure 2). The resulting cell-layer model was then fed input data, and the output data was used to train a deep neural network (DNN). With this reduced-order model, the team was able to quickly gain insight into cell behavior.After training the DNN of the battery model, the team built a custom simulation app to efficiently optimize busbar tabs in the configuration of a battery pack.  Figure 2: The Resolvent battery model.COMSOLA “Tool Within a Tool” for Busbar Weld DesignThe different features of the simulation app, as described by Nielsen, include its options to input dimensions for the pack geometry (Figure 3), the number of cells, and operating conditions such as ambient temperature and charge–discharge current profiles. The app also makes it possible to apply a simple charging current and load customized cycles. Users are then able to see how the battery performs with each set of specific inputs.  Figure 3. The battery pack model developed by Resolvent.COMSOLAnother important aspect of Resolvent’s app is the Busbar Weld Design Tool button, which Nielsen described as “a tool within a tool.” This button can be used to efficiently calculate busbar weld performance after a number of cycles. After clicking the button, a window opens with options for setting different parameters, including the shape of the weld, busbar thickness, and penetration depth of the laser (Figure 4).“[This button] is interesting from a robust design perspective,” said Nielsen. Users can apply a variant to the input parameters to see what happens in production if the weld does not reach far enough into the busbar.  Figure 4. Resolvent’s simulation app, showing how certain parameters can be customized. The model shows how the busbar weld is affected by a cooling airflow.COMSOL“We certainly get deep technical insight here, and we can dimension the design in the sweet spot. Deep technical insight is also key to optimizing product performance,” Nielsen said. For example, if the results suggest better cooling, the team could potentially reduce the design by two battery cells and retain the same performance, easily quantifying the tradeoff between cooling and setup.Predicting Pack PerformanceThe app’s user interface also includes a Compute Battery button, which can be used to see the temperature of the weld in a given state, the state of charge, and the solid–electrolyte interface (SEI) layer thickness (Figure 5). The results can help the engineering team further determine if there is room for optimization in the design. For instance, a user can apply a cooling flow in the app and see if turbulence or standing air occurs.As explained by Nielsen, simulation apps offer more consistent analysis and reporting, and the intuitiveness of custom apps makes it easier to share knowledge. “We are in a much better place to optimize performance and increase robustness,” said Nielsen.  Figure 5. Temperature in the given state (left), state of charge (middle), and SEI layer thickness (right) in the battery pack.COMSOLThe custom simulation app developed by the LaserBATMAN consortium can be used to help produce more robust battery designs with ranges that can support highway travel over longer distances with fewer failures — all while promoting the use of green energy. A heroic project indeed.References“LaserBATMAN,” University of Skovde, accessed 08/21/2025, https://www.his.se/en/research/virtual-engineering/virtual-manufacturing-processes/LaserBatman/.R. Nielsen, “Keynote: Optimizing Lifetime and Robustness of Electric Truck Batteries with Simulation Apps,” COMSOL Conference 2024 Florence, October 2024.

Entertainment.title: Why Denis Villeneuve Needed James Bond to Finally Leave 'Dune' Behind
Entertainment.text: SummaryDenis Villeneuve revealed that signing on to direct the next James Bond film gave him the momentum needed to conclude his 'Dune' trilogyAdapting Frank Herbert’s Dune Messiah the third chapter picks up 17 years later as Paul Atreides succumbs to tyrannical powerWarner Bros will release Dune Part Three in theaters on December 18 2026Warner Bros. and director Denis Villeneuve have shared fresh insight into Dune: Part Three, with the filmmaker revealing how the upcoming James Bond installment serves as his creative escape from the sci-fi franchise. In an interview with Empire, the director reflected candidly on avoiding complacency for the final chapter.Explaining his decision to return to Arrakis, Villeneuve noted that his motivation stemmed from fatigue rather than fond memories. "Maybe it's a good idea to go back to this project, not out of nostalgia, not because I miss it, but the opposite — I'm tired of it," Villeneuve explained. "I want to make sure that I will be severe with the material. That I will not be complacent. I thought, 'When it's done, I need a very powerful rocket to pull me away from Arrakis.' When I was asked to do the next Bond, I said: 'OK, this is what I need.'"Adapting Frank Herbert’s Dune Messiah, the concluding installment jumps 17 years into the future to chronicle Paul Atreides’ (Timothée Chalamet) descent into tyrannical rule. "The idea was to try to make a movie that will have the same DNA — it’s a Dune movie — but it's a very different movie," Villeneuve said. "It has a different pacing. We are back with the same characters, but this time the world has totally changed. Their psyches, their perspective on reality has totally changed, and Paul is living with the burden of what he created, trying to find a way out of this spiral of violence."Dune: Part Three hits theaters on December 18, 2026.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Both offerings arrive in black, keeping the focus on texture and material contrast rather than color, and the jacket is listed at two separate price tiers without further detail on what separates them.WILD THINGS handles the insulation side of the capsule with the Happy Vest, built from a 100% nylon shell packed with PrimaLoft insulation. The sleeveless format keeps the core warm while leaving the arms free, making it a natural layering piece over hoodies or under heavier coats, and it comes in black or gray for a utilitarian finish.For a louder alternative, the Leopard Faux Fur Happy Vest keeps the same PrimaLoft fill but swaps the nylon for a 100% polyester faux fur exterior. The leopard pattern, a recurring WACKO MARIA motif, sits directly on the plush surface, and the vest comes in beige or pink, pushing the outdoor staple firmly into statement territory.The Baracuta and Wild Things x WACKO MARIA FW26 collection is available now via WACKO MARIA stores and authorized stockists, and the WACKO MARIA online store.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: NSQK on 'MOSCA', Kafka, and the Dark Side of Chasing Greatness
Entertainment.text: NSQK was watching his career reach new heights when a mysterious fly infestation turned his apartment into something straight out of a horror movie. As his album ATP gained momentum and bigger stages came into view, the Mexican artist found himself killing up to 20 flies a day in his Monterrey home. What started as a bizarre inconvenience soon became the unlikely foundation for his third studio album, MOSCA.At the time, NSQK was reading Franz Kafka’s The Metamorphosis, a story that began to feel strangely connected to his own life. Between the unexplained infestation, a spiritual cleansing, and the growing pressures of the Latin music industry, he questioned how success seemed to transform him. The flies became a symbol of everything that comes with chasing greatness: envy, ego, criticism, competition, and the constant hunger for more.That tension runs throughout MOSCA. Bringing rock influences into his signature blend of electronic music, pop, and hip-hop, NSQK pushes his sound into new territory across 17 heavy-hitting tracks. Collaborations with Julieta Venegas, Jean Dawson, Eslabón Armado, Kevin Kaarl, and Riosse also mark a shift in his creative process, as he opens the door to more voices and perspectives.We caught up with NSQK to discuss the strange events that inspired MOSCA, the artistic evolution behind his most ambitious record yet, and his plans to bring an entirely new live experience to Mexico City's Estadio GNP Seguros in January 2027.What inspired the title of your new album, MOSCA?“In 2024, I moved into a small apartment in Monterrey with my girlfriend, who is now my wife. We were in the middle of rolling out ATP, we had announced my show at the WTC Pepsi Center in Mexico City, and a lot of exciting things were happening with the project. Everything was really taking off, and suddenly these big, ugly, aggressive green flies started appearing in my apartment.”How did Franz Kafka’s The Metamorphosis influence the concept behind the album?“Around that time, I happened to be reading Kafka’s The Metamorphosis, about a man who wakes up transformed into a giant beetle. I started drawing parallels between that story and what was happening in my career. The project was growing so much, but we were also facing new feelings and experiences within the music industry that we had never encountered before.”How does MOSCA explore the darker side of success and the pressure to keep growing?“The criticism, the comparisons, the envy, and the fear of failure started creeping in. I began connecting all of that to the idea of a metamorphosis, a grotesque transformation into something unrecognizable. That’s what chasing greatness does to you. You constantly want more: more listeners, bigger numbers, more tickets sold, more relevance, better music. That pursuit transforms you, whether you want it to or not.”What happened during your spiritual cleansing that ultimately helped shape the album’s concept?“My manager sent me to get an energy cleansing. I showed up without giving the shaman any context about what was happening in my life or mentioning the flies. When we finished, he told me someone had put a really intense curse on me, fueled by envy, and that it tends to manifest through infestations. I got goosebumps. After that, there were no more flies in my apartment anymore.”How did your approach to making music evolve before and after MOSCA?“What matters to me now is making incredible music, beautiful music, music that will last. I think that’s one of the main reasons I can say I’ve grown musically. It’s about not settling for the first version of something, exploring every possibility, and bringing more people into the process to push the ideas even further.”You recently announced your first show at Mexico City's famous Estadio GNP Seguros. What can fans expect from this milestone performance?“It’s a blessing to perform at Estadio GNP Seguros, not just because of the scale of the venue and the honor of playing a stage like that, but because it allows us to bring our wildest ideas to life. We have an incredible opportunity to go all out, and whenever my team and I get opportunities like this, we make the most of them.”What do you hope listeners take away from MOSCA?“I want people to feel whatever they want to feel and interpret the music however they want. Hopefully, they’ll make beautiful memories with it, at home, with their friends, and at concerts. I want MOSCA to become a part of their lives.” View this post on InstagramA post shared by Hypebeast Latinoamérica (@hypebeastlatam)Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Kim Jones Launches Label & Exits Occur at McQueen & Calvin Klein Collection in This Week's Top Fashion News
Entertainment.text: SummarySeán McGirr exits Alexander McQueen, and Veronica Leoni leaves Calvin Klein Collection.Kim Jones debuts his eponymous fashion label; dunhill heads to Pitti Uomo 111.Tyler, The Creator redesigns FC Barcelona’s kits, while SZA drops her earthy Vans campaign.Kim Jones Announces Eponymous Label With FW27 Debut CollectionAfter much anticipation from fans of the designer, Kim Jones launched a standalone fashion house under his own name. Branching out from his executive tenures at legacy luxury brands like Dior and Fendi, the British designer’s independent label kicks off with a Fall/Winter 2027 collection. Bridging high fashion, streetwear, and utilitarian design, the garments will be primarily crafted in Japan, while the leather accessories will hail from Italy. The inaugural line arrives digitally in mid-2027, with plans for a flagship store opening at Central Yards in Hong Kong that October.McQueen Parts Ways With Creative Director Seán McGirr After Three YearsFollowing a three-year stint at the London label, Seán McGirr officially stepped down as creative director of Alexander McQueen. Parent conglomerate Kering confirmed the departure amidst a broader structural pivot for the brand, which includes staff layoffs and scaling back its 135-store retail footprint. The label recently suffered financial woes driven by over-expansion and a heavy reliance on sneaker sales, which have declined. Brand CEO Luca de Meo emphasized the aim to establish “a bold new direction for the house, building on its unique heritage of exceptional tailoring, uncompromising creativity and rebellion.”Veronica Leoni Steps Down as Creative Director of Calvin Klein CollectionAfter just four seasons, Veronica Leoni concluded her run as the creative director of Calvin Klein Collection. PVH appointed the Céline and The Row alumna in 2024 to resurrect the American brand's premium runway division, which had sat dormant since 2018. Although her minimalist, body-centric vision sparked industry chatter, it failed to generate commercial momentum against a broader 7% quarterly sales dip for Calvin Klein. PVH maintains that the high-end tier remains crucial to its long-term strategy and will announce a replacement in due course.Vans and SZA Unveil California-Shot Campaign for Debut VANSZA Drop 1Vans and SZA showcased the sun-drenched campaign for their inaugural VANSZA collaboration, shot by India Sleem across rugged California landscapes. Dropping October 22, the capsule highlights the singer’s preference for effortless slip-ons through two reworked models: a backless Knu Skool Mule and a distressed Authentic Kickdown featuring a collapsible heel and custom art by Sage Adams. The release rounds out with vintage-inspired outdoor apparel, spanning from oversized outerwear to relaxed cargo pants. SZA is slated to make select in-store appearances to celebrate the launch.Spotify and FC Barcelona Tap Tyler, The Creator and GOLF WANG for El Clásico Jersey Takeover and CollectionFor the latest edition of its FC Barcelona partnership, Spotify granted Tyler, The Creator and his label GOLF WANG full creative control over an FC Barcelona kit takeover. Releasing October 15, the massive lifestyle capsule blends the brand’s playful aesthetic with pitch-ready gear, featuring tracksuits, a letterman jacket, and exactly 1,899 limited-edition retro jerseys. During the highly anticipated El Clásico matchup against Real Madrid on October 25, the signature GOLF logo replaces Spotify’s standard chest branding. A dedicated launch event in Barcelona accompanies the global digital and retail drops.dunhill to Showcase as Guest Designer at Pitti Uomo 111British menswear stalwart dunhill secures the Guest Designer spot for the 111th edition of Pitti Uomo. Scheduled for January 14, 2027, in Florence, the presentation unveils Creative Director Simon Holloway’s Fall/Winter 2027 collection. Mining the cultural crossover of 18th-century British aristocrats touring Italy, the brand represents a refined fusion of classic English tailoring and premier Italian craftsmanship. The invitation marks a significant milestone for dunhill as it continues modernizing its extensive heritage archives on a global stage.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: Craig McDean Celebrates ‘Ducati's 750 Supersport’ in New Tokyo Photography Exhibition
Art & Culture.text: SummaryCraig McDean presents 750 Super Sport, a Ducati-inspired photography exhibition at UNDER R TOKYO.Exclusive merchandise includes graphic T-shirts and long-sleeved tops featuring McDean's motorcycle photography.Running October 23 - November 6, the exhibition also features a photography book.UNDER R, in partnership with Ron Herman, is set to host a photographic exhibition by British fashion photographer Craig McDean this month.Based in New York, McDean first gained recognition through influential publications such as i-D and The Face in the early 1990s before establishing himself as one of fashion photography's leading figures, shooting campaigns and editorials for brands including CHANEL, Jil Sander and Calvin Klein. Titled 750 Super Sport, the exhibition shifts his focus from fashion to the mechanical artistry of Ducati, presenting a series of photographs dedicated to the Italian motorcycle manufacturer's legendary 750 Supersport Green Frame. Accompanied by a photography book of the same name, the project captures the motorcycle's sculptural forms, engineering details and enduring cultural significance, translating its industrial design into a photographic study of craftsmanship and beauty.At the heart of the exhibition is the Ducati 750 Supersport Green Frame, a motorcycle whose origins trace back to the early 1970s. Developed under Ducati chief designer Fabio Taglioni, the 750cc L-twin racing machine made an immediate impact at the 1972 Imola 200, securing first and second place on its debut. Its subsequent road-going iteration became one of the marque's most coveted collector's models, with just 401 examples of the Green Frame produced. Distinguished by its single-seat configuration, open exhaust system, triple disc brakes and desmodromic valve technology, the 1974 model embodied an uncompromising approach to performance and hand-built engineering.Extending the project beyond the gallery, UNDER R has also developed a collaborative apparel capsule featuring short-sleeved and long-sleeved T-shirts in black and white. The short-sleeved designs feature McDean's motorcycle imagery on the front with “750 Super Sport” typography on the reverse, while the long-sleeved versions incorporate a top-down motorcycle photograph alongside printed text and sleeve graphics. Priced at ¥8,800 JPY (approximately $59 USD) and ¥12,100 JPY (approximately $81 USD), respectively, the pieces translate the exhibition's photographic identity into wearable form.The Craig McDean 750 Super Sport Photography Exhibition will run from October 23 through November 6, 2026, at UNDER R TOKYO.UNDER R TOKYO2-6-3 Sendagaya, Shibuya-ku,Tokyo, JapanClick here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: ‘All About Alana’ Charts the Making of an NYC It Girl
Art & Culture.text: Summary'All About Alana,' a new group photo show curated by Ryan McGinley, has opened at Primary Photographic's Rectangle Room in NYCThe exhibition figures actress, model, and musician Alana Jessica Martin through the lens of 30+ notable downtown photographers, exploring the mythology of the muses throughout art history and the role they play in contemporary cultureDating almost as far back as art history is the artist’s muse. One of its more enduring forms in culture is the It Girl, the one who will never wear wrong, always influence, not be influenced. She might not be the first you notice when you walk in a room, but will be the only one you think of when you leave, mastering the kind of elusive cool that won’t ever budge. Every era of New York can be understood by its It’s, Grace Jones, Jenny Shimizu, or Chlöe Sevigny, among them. It's 2026, and a new star has risen.All eyes are on Alana Jessica Martin in a new photo show at Rectangle Room in New York. Curated by Ryan McGinley, All About Alana puts the actress, model, musician, and nightlife darling center stage, tracing the lure of the modern-day muse and her many mythologies.The exhibition features work by over 30 New York-based photographers, spanning selfies, Polaroids, photobooth strips, and gritty black-and-whites, each capturing Martin’s likeness in their own signature styles. One image, the wall-wide opener, channels the drama of a pop confessional, Martin laid bare, with a tear-stained stare locked on the lens; another, high-flashed, sees the artist coolly sipping on Pepsi at Katz’s. Some are explicit in their nod to the other reigning All-American bombshells, with a tattered stripes-and-stars flag high, while Martin stands knee-deep in waves.It’s also a who’s who of downtown photography, so study up, pulling an intergenerational lineup of some of the most exciting image-makers on the scene, such as Daniel Arnold, Charles Caesar, Quil Harwood-Lemons, Jonah Ali Hodari, Jae Kim, Clifford Prince King, Danielle Levitt, Marcus Maddox, Luisa Opalesky, Sam Penn, Richie Shazam, Maxwell Vice and more.All About Alana is now on view at Rectangle Room at Primary Photographic in New York until November 15. Art & Culture.title: Pro Photographer Megan Collante's Latest Shoot Exemplifies Unbreakable Tradition
Art & Culture.text: Toyota has tapped NYC-native photographer Megan Collante to present "A City in Frame: Some Things Never Change," featuring the bZ, part of Toyota’s New All-Electric Family.Since middle school, Kenny and Alex have had a ritual: after school, Alex would be waiting outside by the buses and the two would go get ice cream – no plan, no discussion needed. It's stuck around ever since, even as everything else about their lives changed.Kenny has finally put his brushes down after a 12-hour day in the studio, paint still under his fingernails. His art has only gotten bigger, messier, more demanding as his career has taken off – bigger canvases, later nights, more of himself poured into every piece. But no matter how complicated the day gets, the drive to their spot never does. Alex just puts the bZ in gear and goes, its electrifying performance makes the trip through Manhattan traffic feel effortless and exhilarating, like no time has passed since they were 12 years old. With the touch of a finger, the same playlist they’ve been curating since middle school plays on repeat, turning the bZ into a sanctuary of comfort. And when their one scoop turns into a long night of unwinding through the driving roads near Storm King Mountain, there’s no worry about getting home: miles of charge means a night of memory making.Their tradition bends, but it never breaks.
